source_text: Illae ergo nuptiae quae sine concupiscentia, sine motu corporum, sine necessitate sexuum, ut dicis, esse potuerunt, a te pronuntiantur laudabiles; ista vero coniugia, quae nunc aguntur, a diabolo inventa definis. Illa itaque quae institui potuisse somnias, bona deliberas; ista vero, de quibus dicit Scriptura divina: Relinquet homo patrem et matrem et adhaerebit uxori suae, et erunt duo in carne una 121, profiteris mala diabolica, morbum postremo debere, non coniugium nuncupari
pass_a_gloss: Those marriages therefore which, as you say, could have been without desire, without movement of bodies, without necessity of the sexes, are pronounced praiseworthy by you; but these marriages which are now carried on you define as invented by the devil. Those therefore which you dream could have been instituted you judge good; but these, of which divine Scripture says: A man will leave father and mother and will cling to his wife, and they will be two in one flesh, you profess as diabolical evils, and that at last they ought to be named a disease, not marriage.

lemmas.lexica: LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS nuptiae=nuptials; Blaise Christian marriage good
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: Through what, then, is sin found in the infant? Through the will? The infant had none. Through marriage? But marriage belongs to the parents’ activity, and you had already said that they did not sin in this act—although, from what follows, it appears you had not really granted that. Are the marriages themselves therefore to be cursed because they caused the evil? Yet they indicate only the activity of the persons involved. The parents, then, who caused sin through their union, are rightly subject to condemnation.

If we follow your view, there can now be no doubt that married people are handed over to eternal punishment, since their activity brought about the devil’s rule over human beings. And where is the statement you made a little earlier, that the human being is God’s work? For if evil enters people through their origin, and the devil gains authority over people through that evil, you are calling the devil the maker of human beings, since from him comes the origin of those being born. But if you believe that God makes the human being and that married people are innocent, see how impossible it is to maintain that original sin is derived from them (Genesis 2:24).

choices.why: Julian defends marriage as God's work against the charge that generation transmits sin.
Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's sacred writings; keep Scripture, not 'Bible' as a later book-name.
